publications.title: Statistical Efficiency of Distributional Temporal Difference Learning and Freedman’s Inequality in Hilbert Spaces
publications.abstract:
Distributional reinforcement learning (DRL) has achieved empirical success in various domains. One core task in DRL is distributional policy evaluation, which involves estimating the return distribution η

In this paper, we focus on the non-asymptotic statistical rates of distributional TD learning. To facilitate theoretical analysis, we propose non-parametric distributional TD learning (NTD). This sample complexity bound is minimax optimal up to logarithmic factors. In addition, we revisit categorical distributional TD learning (CTD), showing that the same non-asymptotic convergence bounds hold for CTD. We also extend our analysis to the more general setting where the data-generating process is Markovian. In the Markovian setting, we propose variance-reduced variants of NTD and CTD and show that both can achieve a sample complexity bound matching the state-of-the-art statistical results for classic policy evaluation. We validate our theoretical results through numerical experiments on an inventory management problem, illustrating the practical utility of distributional policy evaluation in risk-sensitive decision-making. To achieve the sharp statistical rates, we establish a novel Freedman’s inequality in Hilbert spaces. This new Freedman’s inequality would be of independent interest for statistical analysis of various infinite-dimensional online learning problems.

publications.title: EXPRESS: Crossing platforms, connecting modalities: A multisource and multimodal interactive neural network for enhanced revenue prediction in service operations
publications.abstract: Demand and revenue prediction is critical in the hotel industry, where fixed capacity and perishable inventory make profitability highly dependent on the effective alignment of pricing, staffing, and procurement decisions with expected market demand and financial outcomes. Accurate forecasts, therefore, serve as a foundation for service operations, enabling managers to balance cost efficiency with service quality. Online reviews have become a valuable source of information for revenue prediction, as they capture customer perceptions of service quality and influence booking intentions. Beyond numerical ratings, reviews often combine textual narratives and visual content, offering rich multimodal signals about customers’ service experiences. Together, these cues provide more comprehensive insights into consumer evaluations than either modality alone. Yet most existing approaches still rely primarily on numerical indicators or text, overlooking both the visual dimension of reviews and the complementary perspectives available across platforms. This narrow focus reduces predictive accuracy and weakens the operational relevance of current models. To address this gap, this paper uses consumer multimodal reviews as the primary data source and examines hotel revenue prediction through the lens of the consumer purchase decision process. We propose a theoretical framework based on this process to guide the design of our prediction model, thereby enhancing the accuracy of RevPAR predictions. The resulting model, termed the multisource and multimodal interactive neural network (MMINN), leverages cross-platform multimodal reviews to predict hotel RevPAR with greater precision. Our findings show that integrating textual and visual information and capturing their interactions improves prediction accuracy. Incorporating cross-platform reviews further enhances predictive power by using a cross-attention mechanism to fuse multisource features. Moreover, focusing on multigranular customer attention-related factors at both the review and platform levels allows the model to capture differences in the informational contributions of different reviews and platforms, which further strengthens revenue prediction. This research provides actionable insights for hotels by supporting revenue management, staffing, marketing, and investment strategies while enhancing competitiveness and customer satisfaction, thereby generating potential economic value for hotels. It also contributes to the service operations and revenue management literature by demonstrating the value of multisource multimodal data integration for advancing revenue prediction.

publications.title: AAE-Desk: Accountable Agentic Evidence Preparation for National Cyber Resilience Governance (Software Prototype, v0.1.0)
publications.abstract: AAE-Desk is a research software prototype that implements the Accountable Agentic Evidence (AAE) model for public administration bodies that prepare decisions on national cyber resilience. It lets software agents discover sources and verify their metadata, while full-text verification, decision making and ex post review remain with named human actors. The software implements: four evidence-preparation functions executed by agents on metadata only: source discovery (F1), provenance verification (F2), appraisal of currency and applicability (F3), and drafting of analytical briefs (F4); three human gates: full-text verification of every claim by an analyst (G1), the decision and its rationale by the accountable official (G2), and ex post review by an oversight forum (G3); an append-only, hash-chained decision record that links each decision back through the brief, claim, verified passage and source record to the original query; a role allocation (RACI) for ten tasks and five actors, in which agents may execute tasks but are never accountable; graduated autonomy zones Z1–Z4 that depend on decision consequence and evidence uncertainty, with escalation triggers; interagency evidence bundles that allow verified evidence to be reused by another agency; indicators from the proposed evaluation design (traceability rate, recall, precision, override patterns, reconstructability); the coding of seven cyber resilience and AI governance frameworks against eight accountability design elements. The deposit contains the Python package (standard library only, Python 3.10+), a web interface and command line, two demonstration scenarios, 30 automated tests, a self-contained Google Colab notebook, and the project description (DOCX). The user interface and documentation are in Ukrainian. Limitations: the agents are deterministic rule-based components, not language models; candidate claims come from a scripted file; discovery uses a local metadata snapshot of 22 records, one of which is synthetic and labelled as such; there is no user authentication. Names of persons and the agency in the demonstration scenarios are fictitious. Demonstration indicators are illustrative and do not constitute empirical evidence for the propositions of the underlying study.

publications.title: Column Elimination: An Iterative Approach to Solving Arc-Flow Formulations
publications.abstract: We present column elimination as a general framework for solving problems whose solutions can be represented as a collection of decision sequences. We show how such problems can be modeled as arc-flow formulations, using a dynamic program to represent the set of feasible decision sequences and their costs, and an integer linear program over the corresponding state-transition graph. Because the exact arc-flow formulation can be exponentially large, we introduce relaxed dynamic programs to compactly represent a superset of the feasible decision sequences. Column elimination solves the exact model by starting with a relaxed dynamic program, which induces a relaxed arc-flow formulation, and iteratively refining the relaxation by eliminating infeasible sequences in optimal solutions. Doing so, we generalize earlier approaches that were developed for decision-diagram based network models. We apply our general column elimination framework to three new applications: the vehicle routing problem with time windows, the pickup-and-delivery problem with time windows, and the graph multicoloring problem. The computational results show that column elimination is competitive with or outperforms state-of-the-art methods, closing several previously open benchmark instances across these domains, including one vehicle routing problem with time windows on 1,000 locations.

publications.title: Dual Active Learning for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
publications.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences is critical to recent advances in generative artificial intelligence. Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is widely applied to achieve this objective. A key step in RLHF is to learn the reward function from human feedback. However, human feedback is costly and time-consuming, making it essential to collect high-quality conversation data for human teachers to label. Additionally, different human teachers have different levels of expertise. It is thus critical to query the most appropriate teacher for their opinions. In this paper, we use offline reinforcement learning (RL) to formulate the alignment problem. Motivated by the idea of $D$-optimal design, we first propose a dual active reward learning algorithm for the simultaneous selection of conversations and teachers. Next, we apply pessimistic RL to solve the alignment problem, based on the learned reward estimator. Theoretically, we show that the reward estimator obtained through our proposed adaptive selection strategy achieves minimal generalized variance asymptotically, and prove that the sub-optimality of our pessimistic policy scales as $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ with a given sample budget $T$. Through simulations and experiments on LLMs, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm and its superiority over state-of-the-art.

publications.title: EXPRESS: A Framework Addressing Supply Chain Carbon Emissions: Measurement, Reporting, and Reduction
publications.abstract: This paper honors Professor Christopher S. Tang’s seminal contributions to sustainable operations management by examining the pivotal yet underappreciated role of supply chains in global carbon emissions. Despite the critical importance of supply chains in contributing to overall carbon footprints, current efforts to address these emissions are often overshadowed by more visible direct emissions (Scope 1) and energy-related emissions (Scope 2). To bridge this gap, we propose an integrated measurement-reporting-reduction framework for managing supply chain carbon emissions (upstream Scope 3). Drawing on the literature, we introduce methodologies for carbon measurement (e.g., EEIO models, LCA, machine learning, and blockchain), determinants and consequences of disclosure, and strategies for reduction. In addition, we present case studies of two industrial firms, Tongwei (a Chinese photovoltaic leader) and Siemens (a German multinational technology firm), to illustrate how firms with distinct institutional contexts implement the framework in practice, highlighting the strengths, challenges, and implications. We conclude with research questions on whether disclosure mandates and carbon border measures lead to real abatement or merely shift emissions across suppliers and borders.

publications.title: Estimating malaria burden in sub-Saharan Africa under intervention disruption using satellite-derived representations
publications.abstract: Abstract Malaria remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. Stalled progress and funding constraints raise important questions about the dependence of current malaria burden on sustained intervention coverage. Here, we estimate malaria transmission potential under a low-intervention scenario where major malaria interventions are withdrawn while broader ecological and demographic conditions remain constant. We develop a contrastive representation-learning framework applied to 30-m Landsat 8 satellite imagery, integrating the resulting environmental representations within a Bayesian hierarchical model. This approach improves predictive accuracy over existing covariate-based malaria mapping methods. Using contemporary Global Burden of Disease 2024 population estimates, we estimate an annual malaria burden of 422 (275-582) million cases across sub-Saharan Africa, representing a 131% increase relative to current estimates. These findings quantify the structural vulnerability of malaria control gains across sub-Saharan Africa and reveal where intervention disruption could have the greatest impact.

publications.title: NYMPHE Ecological Search: a portable index and retrieval package for 64 ecological datasets
publications.abstract: A portable, English-language software and data-access package for searching 64 published NYMPHE ecological datasets. It includes an offline-ready browser interface, a weighted BM25 keyword index, equivalent Python command-line retrieval, a catalog of 64 distinct dataset DOIs, and instructions for installation, local running, automated parsing and index rebuilding. The fixed source snapshot dated 18 November 2026 contains 505 unchanged primary CSV records and 633 retrievable documents: 64 dataset summaries, 505 source rows and 64 methods/limitations records. Search results preserve individual dataset creators, source-row identifiers, literal values, rights and DOI citations. Every primary CSV matches the MD5 retained in its publication receipt. Source observations, derived descriptors, protocols and reference material retain distinct interpretation labels. The browser application can search without an LLM, API key, external service or internet connection; following external DOI links requires internet access. Search is lexical, with exact-token phrases and filters for site, study context, dataset, field and content type. This release does not include embeddings, a generative model, model training or ecological trend analysis. Erpe, Falasarna, ENI Rewind/Ferrara and Otos share one field-baseline campaign spanning confirmed visits in 2024–2026. CENVIS is a separate 2026 mesocosm feasibility experiment. Context periods do not invent individual row dates. Excluded tables and externally owned environment/ecotoxicology material are not included. Validation includes 22 Python acceptance tests, 22 JavaScript/Python retrieval-parity cases, 18 simulated-DOM checks, JSON Schema validation and deterministic rebuilding. Interactive real-browser rendering and the localhost server were not tested end-to-end in the restricted build environment. Source-draft scientific limitations remain applicable. Software authors, in citation order: Florin Alexandru; Gabriela Staicu; Mara Alexandru. Owner and rights holder: ADEMED — Association for Development and Environment. AI assistance disclosure: The software was developed with assistance from OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex, based on GPT-6. AI assistance was used for architecture, implementation, documentation and automated-test preparation. The named human authors are responsible for reviewing and approving the released work; the AI tool is acknowledged as assistance and is not an author. Horizon Europe funding acknowledgment: Funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under grant agreement No 101060625 (NYMPHE). The authors acknowledge the support of the European Commission, the funder identified in the NYMPHE grant record. Views and opinions expressed are those of the author(s) only and do not necessarily reflect those of the European Union or the granting authority. Neither the European Union nor the granting authority can be held responsible for them. Licensing: newly written application code and tools use the MIT License. The source datasets, catalog, derived index and documentation use Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Retain the individual dataset citations. The EU emblem and funding banner are excluded from the data license. Use: extract the complete ZIP and open index.html. Optional Python tools require Python 3.10 or later and no additional packages. The 64-source catalog and all metadata are bundled for robotic parsing. The source datasets remain independently citable research outputs; this software record is an additional access and retrieval resource.

publications.title: Sonicium Function-Calling Series: 50 Synthetic Tool-Use Datasets for LLM Agents
publications.abstract: Created by Hussain Billah (ORCID 0009-0009-5686-619X) · Published by Sonicium Quantum Lab Ltd. This record is the data card and catalog of the Sonicium Function-Calling Series: a collection of 50 synthetic function-calling (tool-use) datasets, one per service domain (banking, flights, hotel booking, e-commerce, healthcare appointments, smart home and more). Every record is a full tool-use episode: system prompt, available tools as JSON schemas (including distractor tools), user request, reasoning note, expected tool call with arguments, simulated tool result and final answer, plus difficulty, split and a reproducible generator seed. The series contains 50 datasets (about 3,848,300 records in total). The full data of each dataset is hosted on Kaggle; catalog.csv lists every dataset with its Kaggle URL, size and record count, and README.md is the series data card. All data was produced by deterministic, seeded Python generators written by Sonicium Quantum Lab Ltd.; no LLM was used to write the data. Released under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; commercial licenses and custom datasets are available on request. Contact: Nazmul Basher (Head of Marketing & Communications), research@sonicium.ltd · collaboration@sonicium.ltd · https://soniciumquantumlab.com

publications.title: Beam Model Technical Report
publications.abstract: Beam is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 501.3B total parameters and 23.4B active parameters, specifically built and optimized for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. Beam delivers frontier level reasoning, while requiring 3-4x less inference compute than many models of its class. Pretrained on 23.8T diverse, curated, high-quality tokens, Beam features a 1M-token context window achieved through a novel two-stage midtraining phase, built on verifiable, correctness-anchored data. Post-training leveraged a large-scale, fully asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) campaign across 10.5K GB300 GPUs, generating over 100M rollouts over 4 weeks of training. We believe this is one of the largest scale RL runs conducted by any open lab to date. Across our evaluation suite, capabilities continued to improve as we increased RL compute, with no sign of a plateau. Supported by deep hardware-model co-design, FP8/NVFP4 quantization, and a 1.93B-parameter speculative decoding drafter (DFlash 2), Beam maximizes serving throughput with efficient, flexible deployment. Averaged across conversation turns and harm categories, Beam refuses or pivots on 88.9% of harmful requests while complying with 81.5% of harmless requests, achieving the highest refusal/pivot rate on harmful requests among open-weight models on the Pareto frontier.
